articles.title: BRICS issues New Delhi Declaration, as UAE and Iran back down from tough positions - The Hindu
articles.description: The BRICS bloc adopted the 'New Delhi Declaration' during its latest summit, emphasizing resilience, innovation, cooperation, and sustainability. India played a pivotal diplomatic role in bridging differences between newly added members, Iran and the United Arab Emirates (UAE), to achieve full consensus. The declaration focuses on multilateral reform, economic integration, counter-terrorism, and strengthening regional stability. For competitive exams, note the expansion of BRICS (originally Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa) to include new members like the UAE, Iran, Egypt, and Ethiopia.

articles.title: India’s central bank tells Tata Sons to take conglomerate public - Financial Times
articles.description: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) rejected Tata Sons' application to surrender its Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC) license, mandating its public listing. Under RBI's Scale Based Regulation (SBR) framework introduced in 2021, Tata Sons is classified as an 'Upper Layer' NBFC (NBFC-UL) due to its systemic importance. NBFC-UL entities are subject to enhanced regulatory oversight and must mandatorily list on stock exchanges within three years of identification to ensure greater transparency, corporate governance, and financial stability in India's shadow banking sector.

articles.title: India rules out Brics currency proposal, backs local currency trade settlements - The Times of India
articles.description: India has officially ruled out proposals for a common BRICS currency, advocating instead for national currency trade settlements to facilitate international commerce. While supporting de-dollarisation and global financial reforms, India emphasizes strengthening local currency cross-border payment systems (like UPI-based linkages and Special Vostro Rupee Accounts). This approach aims to reduce transaction costs and currency volatility without creating a rigid monetary union. Additionally, the stance highlights India's push for reforming voting quotas and governance structures in international financial institutions like the IMF and World Bank.

articles.title: DFCs: The backbone of India’s logistics push
articles.description: The Western Dedicated Freight Corridor (WDFC) has become fully operational, establishing a 2,843-km dedicated rail network with the Eastern DFC (EDFC) to transform national logistics. Executed by the Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited (DFCCIL) under the Ministry of Railways, DFCs are designed to segregate freight movement from passenger traffic. This infrastructure milestone supports the National Logistics Policy, aiming to reduce India's logistics costs from 13–14% of GDP to single digits, enhance freight train speeds, and boost industrial corridors.

articles.title: India and EU close to sealing trade deal, await nod from top Council in Brussels - The Indian Express
articles.description: India and the European Union (EU) are nearing finalization of a landmark Free Trade Agreement (FTA), pending approval from the European Council in Brussels. Negotiations encompass three main pillars: trade in goods and services, investment protection, and Geographical Indications (GIs). The EU remains one of India's largest trade partners and investors. Key discussion areas include lowering tariffs on automobiles and spirits, market access, regulatory alignment, and addressing EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) to boost bilateral trade resilience.

articles.title: Asia Cup: Indian women's cricket team refuses to accept trophy from ACC head Mohsin Naqvi
articles.description: The Indian women’s cricket team, led by Captain Harmanpreet Kaur, secured their record-extending eighth Women's Asia Cup title by defeating Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the final. The Asian Cricket Council (ACC), established in 1983 to promote and develop cricket across Asia, organizes the tournament. The event highlights India's dominance in regional women's cricket. For competitive exams, key facts include India's 8th title win, ACC headquarters in Dubai, UAE, and the role of ACC under the International Cricket Council (ICC) framework.

articles.title: S-400 destroyed Pakistani aircraft at 314 km during Operation Sindoor: Defence Ministry report - thehindu.com
articles.description: According to a Ministry of Defence report, India's S-400 air defense system successfully engaged and destroyed a target at a range of 314 km during Operation Sindoor. The S-400 Triumf is a mobile, surface-to-air missile (SAM) system developed by Russia's Almaz-Antey, capable of intercepting aircraft, drones, and ballistic missiles up to 400 km. Acquired under an intergovernmental agreement signed between India and Russia in 2018, the system significantly enhances the Indian Air Force’s (IAF) long-range air defense capabilities and integrated air command network.

articles.title: UCC in all 21 NDA-ruled States by 2029: Amit Shah - thehindu.com
articles.description: Union Home Minister Amit Shah announced the implementation of the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) across all 21 NDA-ruled states by 2029. UCC is enshrined under Article 44 of Part IV (Directive Principles of State Policy) of the Indian Constitution, which mandates the state to secure a uniform set of civil laws governing marriage, divorce, inheritance, and adoption for all citizens regardless of religion. Uttarakhand recently became the first post-independence Indian state to pass a UCC bill, setting a legal precedent for state-level implementations.

articles.title: India to get 1.64 million-tonne EU steel quota; 6.95 lakh tonnes under FTA - Moneycontrol.com
articles.description: Under ongoing negotiations for the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement (FTA), India has secured a 1.64 million-tonne annual steel quota, including 6.95 lakh tonnes under preferential FTA terms. The proposed agreement also allows the import of 1,000,000 cars from the EU at reduced tariff rates during its initial year. Overseen by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, the trade deal aims to enhance bilateral commerce, ease tariff barriers, and expand Indian steel exports, while addressing European Union trade safeguard measures and carbon import regulations.

articles.title: Brics opposes unilateral trade steps like EU carbon border tax - The Times of India
articles.description: The BRICS bloc voiced strong opposition to unilateral trade restrictions, specifically targeting the European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM). BRICS members argued that such carbon border taxes violate World Trade Organization (WTO) norms and the principle of Common But Differentiated Responsibilities (CBDR) under the UNFCCC. Instead, the grouping advocated for voluntary carbon market cooperation and climate finance for developing nations. The development highlights rising trade tensions over green protectionism and its impact on emerging economies' industrial exports, including Indian steel and aluminum.

articles.title: Govt. bars bank charges on payments up to ₹2,000 via UPI, RuPay-powered debit cards
articles.description: The Union Government has prohibited banks from levying charges or Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on transactions up to ₹2,000 executed via Unified Payments Interface (UPI) and RuPay debit cards. Issued under amendments to the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, this decision aims to boost digital payments penetration across small merchants. Developed by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) in 2016, UPI operates under RBI guidelines. This zero-MDR mandate supports financial inclusion while strengthening digital financial infrastructure.

articles.title: India approves expedited export of electricity to flood-hit Nepal
articles.description: The Union Ministry of Power approved the expedited export of electricity to flood-hit Nepal to meet its urgent energy demands. Managed under Cross-Border Electricity Trade (CBET) guidelines, the initiative highlights India’s Neighborhood First policy and bilateral energy cooperation. Central Electricity Authority (CEA) acts as the designated authority for cross-border power trade approvals. India and Nepal share sub-regional energy integration mechanisms, including power purchase agreements and joint hydro-project initiatives like the Arun-III power project, reinforcing regional power grid connectivity.

articles.title: Pakistan names Jaish chief Masood Azhar among most wanted terrorists, hikes bounty to PKR 70 lakh ahead of FATF review | World News - Hindustan Times
articles.description: Pakistan announced a bounty of PKR 70 lakh for Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) chief Masood Azhar ahead of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) plenary review. Azhar was designated a global terrorist by the UN Security Council’s 1267 Sanctions Committee in May 2019. FATF, established in 1989 by G7 countries and headquartered in Paris, monitors global money laundering and terror financing. Countries non-compliant with FATF anti-money laundering standards face placement on the Grey or Black Lists, incurring severe international financial restrictions.

articles.title: India, Canada begin next round of talks on proposed trade pact: Official
articles.description: India and Canada initiated negotiations for an Early Progress Trade Agreement (EPTA) as a step toward a full Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA). Overseen by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, the trade pact aims to expand bilateral trade to $50 billion by 2030. Key focus areas include pharmaceuticals, clean energy, agriculture, critical minerals, and services. Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) like CEPA lower tariff barriers, boost bilateral investments, and facilitate trade integration between negotiating partner nations.

articles.title: WPI inflation rises to 9.92% in August on rising prices of food, fuel, manufactured items
articles.description: India's Wholesale Price Index (WPI) inflation rose to 9.92% in August, driven by surges in food, fuel, and manufactured items, which hit a series high of 8.37%. WPI measures wholesale price changes and is published monthly by the Office of the Economic Adviser, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, with 2011-12 as its base year. The index comprises Primary Articles (22.62%), Fuel and Power (13.15%), and Manufactured Products (64.23%). Unlike CPI, WPI excludes service sector inflation.

articles.title: Decoding India’s GDP base revision
articles.description: India's Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) periodically revises the base year for Gross Domestic Product (GDP) calculations to better reflect structural shifts in the economy. A major driver for upcoming revisions is the enhanced statistical coverage and improved measurement of the unorganized and unincorporated services sector. Updating base years aligns GDP estimates with international System of National Accounts (SNA) standards, capturing updated consumption patterns and new economic activities for precise macroeconomic policy formulation by the government and the RBI.

articles.title: Six States, UT sign Kishau multipurpose project agreement; CM Sukhu hails ‘major victory’ for Himachal
articles.description: Six beneficiary states/UTs—including Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Haryana, Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, and Rajasthan—have signed an agreement for the Kishau Multipurpose Project. Located on the Tons River, a major tributary of the Yamuna River along the Uttarakhand-Himachal Pradesh border, this 660 MW hydro-electric project aims to generate power and provide irrigation and drinking water. Classified as a Project of National Importance, the central government funds 90% of the water component, enhancing inter-state water sharing, regional power grid supply, and flood moderation capabilities.

articles.title: August retail inflation raises chances of RBI rate hike in October, say economists
articles.description: India's retail inflation, measured by the Consumer Price Index (CPI) released by the National Statistical Office (NSO), rose to a 20-month high of 4.8% in August, driven primarily by surging food prices. Under the Monetary Policy Framework, the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) targets headline CPI inflation at 4% with a tolerance band of 2% to 6%. Rising inflationary pressures restrict the central bank's room for monetary easing and increase the likelihood of benchmark repo rate hikes to anchor inflation expectations.

articles.title: Expect EU to sign FTA and India-Canada negotiations to be completed by year-end, govt says
articles.description: The Union Ministry of Commerce and Industry announced significant progress in India's bilateral trade negotiations, expecting the completion of negotiations with Canada and major strides on the India-EU Free Trade Agreement (FTA). Additionally, trade talks with the U.S. focus on resolving bilateral tariff issues and finalizing a long-delayed interim trade agreement. FTAs aim to reduce tariff barriers, expand market access for Indian goods and services, streamline supply chains, and boost foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows across crucial industrial and service sectors.

articles.title: India’s 26% goods exports surge lowers August 2026 trade deficit
articles.description: According to the Department of Commerce, India's merchandise exports witnessed a robust 26% growth, outpacing import growth in both percentage and absolute terms to significantly narrow the trade deficit. The surge was driven by high demand in key engineering, petroleum, chemical, and electronics sectors. The trade deficit—the difference between the monetary value of merchandise imports and exports—directly influences the Current Account Deficit (CAD). Strong foreign trade metrics help bolster foreign exchange reserves and strengthen the Indian Rupee against macroeconomic volatility.
